Meaning: To represent with a symbol.
Example: We denote a percentage by x%.

Meaning: Any at all; chosen freely.
Example: If a, b and c are arbitrary numbers…

Meaning: Zero or positive.
Example: If a and b are non-negative numbers…

Meaning: To be true.
Example: This rule holds for all real numbers.

Meaning: To bring a reward later.
Example: The work you put in now will pay dividends later.
Note: Figurative here, not the finance term.

Meaning: How fast one quantity changes as another changes.
Example: The derivative is a rate of change.

Meaning: In relation to; measuring against.
Example: Differentiate with respect to x.

Meaning: Something that MUST be true, but may not be enough on its own.
Example: f'(c) = 0 is a necessary condition for a maximum.

Meaning: Something that is ENOUGH to guarantee a result.
Example: FOC plus SOC together are sufficient.
Note: necessary ≠ sufficient. Examiners love this pair.

Meaning: To check that something is true.
Example: To verify this is a maximum, take the second derivative.

Meaning: To find the value of a particular unknown.
Example: Set it equal to zero and solve for q.

Meaning: To go up / to go down.
Example: A function may be increasing for some values of x.

Meaning: Going up from left to right / going down.
Example: The graph of the first derivative is downward-sloping.

Meaning: To work out the numerical value.
Example: Use the Fundamental Theorem to evaluate the integral.

Meaning: The two end values a and b of a definite integral.
Example: The limits are written above and below the integral sign.

Meaning: The space between a graph and the horizontal axis.
Example: The definite integral gives the area under the curve.

Meaning: With no breaks or jumps.
Example: Let f(x) and g(x) be continuous functions.

Meaning: Able to be asked about in the exam.
Example: Several integration slides are marked "not examinable".
Note: Check this word on every slide. It saves you work.

Meaning: Money received or paid at a point in time.
Example: A project generates cash flows cᵢ at time i.

Meaning: The money you pay out at the start.
Example: An initial outlay of $50,000.

Meaning: A standard you compare against.
Example: The required rate of return is the benchmark.

Meaning: To take on / to turn down.
Example: Accept the project if IRR > required return.
Note: The decision pair for NPV and IRR questions.

Meaning: Constant; the same each period.
Example: An annuity is a series of level cash flows.

Meaning: To miss out.
Example: In an annuity, none is skipped.

Meaning: The original sum borrowed or lent.
Example: For a Consol bond, the principal is never repaid.
Note: NOT "principal" as in main, and not the IC101 "principal" intermediary.

Meaning: To think about; to treat as.
Example: A matrix is considered as one mathematical object.

Meaning: All at the same time.
Example: A solution satisfies all the equations simultaneously.

Meaning: In the order just mentioned.
Example: Returns in year 1 and 2 are $30,000 and $40,000 respectively.
Note: Very common in exam questions. Read carefully.

Meaning: To make it clearer.
Example: For clarity, we show the order below the matrix.

Meaning: To depend on.
Example: Many future courses rely upon the foundations built here.
